attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Present-tense capability claim. The 'as tasks get more complex' qualifier is kept. Narrowing 'all LLMs' to coding LLMs fits the coding context.

contract.note: Zitron gave no complexity measure, no definition of hallucination and no period, so the evaluator supplied all three. Requiring hallucinations to be measured separately from failures follows his words. The September 2025 window is reasonable.

evidence.note: Shows that library hallucinations persist and vary with how prompts are worded. It does not measure hallucination rates against task complexity.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no evaluation that measures task complexity, failures and hallucinations together for contemporary coding models. The only item shows that hallucinations exist and are sensitive to prompts. It does not show a gradient with complexity, so the evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own conclusion, drawn after he cites several cost estimates.

semantics.note: In context, the claim is that $10bn does not cover the full cost of building and equipping a 1GW data center. The normalised proposition preserves that.

contract.note: Measuring total capital cost per fully equipped GW is an ordinary reading of his words. The contract also correctly avoids treating $10bn as unable to start construction or to attract further financing.

evidence.note: Reuters, Sept 23, 2025: Huang's estimate of about $50bn per GW, which leaves about $40bn beyond the $10bn. The figure is a reported estimate from Nvidia's CEO.
Morning Brew, Sept 25, 2025, reporting OpenAI's figure of about $50bn per gigawatt. It corroborates the estimate but is not independent of the company.
The $10bn was meant to help secure more financing. This is about OpenAI's funding structure, not the total project cost.

reviews.rationale: Estimates reported in September 2025, from Nvidia's CEO via Reuters and from OpenAI via Morning Brew, put a fully equipped 1GW facility at about $50bn, roughly five times $10bn. These are estimates, not audited budgets, but the contract allows that. The financing point in e3 does not lower the total cost.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. The Carl Brown quote is in the previous sentence, not this one.

semantics.note: An unqualified general claim about what coding LLMs do to engineers' speed. Treating it as causal is correct.

contract.note: Reading the sentence as general is the plain reading, since it states no restriction. Measuring completion time in controlled studies is fair. A mixed result when credible studies conflict is reasonable.

evidence.note: METR randomized trial: experienced open-source maintainers took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools.
Randomized trial of 96 Google engineers on an enterprise task: about 21% less time with AI. The confidence interval is wide.

reviews.rationale: The slowdown holds in one credible setting: experienced maintainers working on mature open-source projects in early 2025 (METR). The unconditional claim that the tools do not speed engineers up is contradicted by a randomized trial that found Google engineers finished an enterprise task about 21% faster. Populations and tools differ between the studies.

attribution.note: Zitron's own framing statement in the essay.

semantics.note: 'I see no future beyond' is firm, unhedged language predicting eventual collapse. The 'fiery apocalypse' metaphor is kept, and there is no deadline.

contract.note: Reading the metaphor as an industry-wide financial collapse is an ordinary reading. Because there is no deadline, the contract allows only early resolution in Zitron's favour, which suits an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own May 2026 statement about expanding compute. A company disclosure, and it cannot refute a forecast with no deadline.
Anthropic's own Oct 27, 2026 statement about government adoption. Ongoing activity, but not a test of eventual collapse.

reviews.rationale: This is a forecast with no deadline. No dated event in the packet meets the early-resolution rule of an industry-wide collapse, and continued activity by leading firms cannot disprove an eventual-collapse forecast. It stays unresolved.
